main_text.p: 2.Cor.3.5.Ioh.15.5.Et Rom. 14: Quicquid non est ex fide peccatum est.
Ratio: quia fingit hanc tantum esse illius [?]σεοπ[?]- [?]νευστιν [?]: & quidem coram Deo.
I. In genere: quod justificatio sit relationis: regeneratio alterationis.
II. In forma, quòd illa sit imputatio justitiæ Christi'per fidem : hæc instauratio naturæ per Spiritum S.
III. In ordine : quod tempore quidem sint simul: sed illa hanc præcedat naturâ.
IV. Ingradibus : quod illa perfecta sit in hac vita. Rom.8.1. 1.Ioh.1.7. Hæc tantum incoata & semper crescens: quod sensus, querelæ, & preces sanctorum testantur.
Addatur hic [illegible, ~7 letters] de necessitate discrimi-nis: ne obscuretur gratia Christi:& labefactetur consolatio Evangelii in judicio Dei.
Quinto: Falsò statuit Paulum tantum adimere justificationem operibus ante gratiam.
Probetur: quia adimit eam etiam operibus Abrahami renati. Rom.4.2. Et ex antithesi gratiæ atque operum. Rom.11.6.
Conclusio habeat [?]συλλογισμὸν[?]. Nollete sophisma-tum pontificiorum de Iustificatione operum re-futationem addere.
Ratio 1. ne prolixitas materiæ tædium affe-rat.

page.notes: The Greek word after "illius" (two lines, ending "-" and "...") is only partly legible; it is written with [?] and needs checking against the scan. The Greek word after "Conclusio habeat" is a guess at συλλογισμὸν and is marked [?]. The Greek word after "hic" is illegible. A stray vertical mark "|" stands after "naturâ." and is left out of the text. "Christi'per" has an apostrophe as printed. At the lower right, "II." stands before the catchword "Quia"; it is not transcribed as a signature.
